source.title: Compositional Literary Primitives in Instruction-Tuned LLMs: Cross-Architectural SAE Features for Self, Style, and Affect
source.citation: J. P. C. Presa et al., 2026
source.authors: J. P. C. Presa; S. D. de Oliveira

record.file_problem: The text is substantially readable and includes the full paper and supplementary material, though some PDF/OCR equation and table formatting is corrupted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests the LLM-specific indirect-evidence version by recovering and steering SAE features in two instruction-tuned LLMs. It applies feature analysis in a new setting rather than reproducing the original toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-feature discovery and causal steering in Llama and Gemma, which bear on whether SAEs recover usable features in LLMs. It does not test superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance as determinants of geometry, neuron-level polysemanticity, or multidimensional features. Prompt templates and instructions for judge models are experimental materials, not instructions addressed to an AI reviewing this text.
record.test_reason: The paper uses public SAEs (Llama Scope, Gemma Scope) as a tool to catalogue emotion, self and style features, and reports how well its own discovery-and-steering pipeline works. It does not test superposition geometry, capacity-driven polysemanticity, how features spread across neurons, or how sparse the features are. The steering hit rates are for the best candidates its search selected, not a measure of whether dictionaries recover a model's features. The closest it comes to a claim version is its observation that some SAE features play several context-dependent roles, which bears on monosemanticity rather than on V5's completeness, stability or canonicality. That finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors claim instruction-tuned LLMs encode literary craft principles (show-don't-tell, emotion naming, voice) as separable, steerable, compositional SAE features in four classes. They report Llama reaching 27/27 and Gemma 23/27 Cowen-Keltner coverage under forced-choice judging, and they propose their three-stage validation pipeline as canonical. They also note that features can be multi-role and that the catalogs are not exhaustive. The conclusion's item 2 says suppression releases affect, which contradicts §5.2 (single-feature suppression does not; only joint steering does).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive prompt corpora, SAE feature discovery and decoder-direction steering in instruction-tuned LLMs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition setup. The paper reports code and data artifacts, but no release URL in the text.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with steering coefficient, feature choice, prompt context, and judge criterion. The paper reports α-dependent emotion shifts and drift, context-dependent feature roles, and differences between strict and soft judging.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama, a single SAE feature (f32213) acts as a show-don't-tell modulator on scene prompts and as a self-register on identity probes at the same α. Several self-features also act as emotion emitters (f96419 disgust; Gemma f70443 fear).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual SAE features in instruction-tuned LLMs can play several context-selected roles (not one feature, one role).

fits_no_version.finding: Some emotions (joy, adoration in Llama) were reached only by jointly steering several SAE features. In Gemma, joy is reached by a singleton feature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some concepts are not captured by any single SAE feature and appear only as combinations, which differ across models.

record.problems: Only two models are studied; per-cell sample sizes are generally 2–7 seeds. The authors note that human calibration of the LLM-judge panel is incomplete, random-feature controls are not exhaustive, and some outputs judged as target emotion are incoherent or code-switch. Several reported effects are small-sample judge outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the cross-lingual gate results in §7 and §A.8, additional alternative gates and alpha-sweep cells in §§3–6, and supplementary judge-criterion reratings beyond the CK-27 aggregate in Table 6. The retained rows focus on the main SAE feature catalogs and the directly reported multifunctional feature result.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature-versus-dimension sweeps, sparsity transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No polysemantic neurons or non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Neither feature spreading across neurons nor whether SAEs recover sparse features is tested; SAEs are used as given tools.
Completeness, stability across SAE training runs or widths, and canonicality are not tested.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests call was rejected because the steering results are selected-candidate pipeline outcomes on public SAEs, with no test of superposition or dictionary recovery itself. No α=0 per-cell baselines are given, sample sizes are 2–7 seeds, and there is no human evaluation. Judge-template descriptions are internally inconsistent (§3.4 vs §A.5).

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network feature-over-dimension sweep, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric arrangement is tested.
No neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, dedicated-dimension allocation, or importance-dependent sharing is tested.
The paper reports multifunctional SAE features, but does not study polysemantic neurons or test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-recoverable and steerable features in two instruction-tuned LLMs. Does not test feature distribution across neurons or measure how sparse the recovered features are.

Tests whether some feature roles remain exclusive across contexts, finding role overlap/context dependence. Does not establish completeness, stability across training runs, or canonicality of SAE features as the model's full representational units.
Uses individual SAE decoder directions for steering but does not compare 1-D features with multidimensional features or test whether the represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional.
